newsitem.title: FRANCE: Gunman releases 35 hostages in central Paris.
newsitem.headline: Gunman releases 35 hostages in central Paris.

text.p: A disgruntled former bank employee armed with a pistol held 35 people hostage for two hours, slightly wounding two of them, at the bank's office in central Paris on Friday, police said.
The unnamed 55-year-old man was detained after releasing the hostages.
"Everyone has been freed. The hostage-taker has been apprehended," a police spokeswoman told Reuters by telephone.

Police said the gunman seized the hostages at around 1 p.m. (1200 GMT) at the offices of his former employer, a private investment bank on the third floor of a building on the busy downtown Boulevard Haussmann, in the capital's eighth district.
The gunman shot two of the hostages. He later released them and they were taken to hospital, where they were reported to be in satisfactory condition.
The avenue was quickly cordoned off and police and emergency services were called to the scene.
The gunman later freed 32 more hostages, then released the last one at around 3 p.m. (1400 GMT).
